question: What was Sartre's opinion on his novel which included the character The Autodidact?
final_answer: The Autodidact is a fictional character in Nausea, and Sartre considered it one of his best works. He believed that self instruction is of critical importance to him, and provides the explanation for his odd behavior and continual self-delusion.

results.title: John Lockman
results.text: Born in humble circumstances, he was an autodidact scholar who learnt to speak French by frequenting Slaughter's Coffee House. He had enough acquaintance with Alexander Pope that he could dedicate to him in 1734 his translation of Charles Porée's "Oration". His inoffensive character procured for him the name of the ‘Lamb.’ but when ‘Hesiod’ Cooke abused his poetry, Lockman retorted, ‘It may be so; but, thank God! my name is not at full length in the “Dunciad. ”’
